title: Attaching & Detaching: `docker attach` 🔗
description: Connect your terminal to a container’s main process and detach safely.

slides.title: What is `docker attach`? 🔄
slides.content:
# Connect to PID 1

`docker attach` hooks your terminal’s **STDIN, STDOUT and STDERR** to the container’s **main process** (PID 1).

```bash
docker attach [OPTIONS] CONTAINER
```

Unlike `docker exec` (which starts a new process), `attach` connects to the already‑running main process.

This is how `docker run` works in attached mode by default (without `-d`).

slides.title: Attach vs Exec – Key Differences ⚖️
slides.content:
| Feature          | `docker exec`                     | `docker attach`                      |
|------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| New process?     | Yes, a new command                | No, uses existing PID 1              |
| Shell available? | Yes, with `-it bash`             | Only if PID 1 is a shell             |
| Detaching        | `exit` or `Ctrl+D`               | `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+Q` (detach without stopping) |
| Use case         | Debugging, maintenance            | Watching real‑time logs of PID 1     |

> `attach` is rarely used today; `exec` and `docker logs -f` are more flexible.

quizData.question: You want to get a Bash shell inside a running container. Which command should you use?
quizData.explanation: `exec` creates a new Bash process. `attach` would only work if the main process was already a shell.

slides.title: Detaching Safely ✂️
slides.content:
# The Magic Key Sequence

When you are attached with `docker attach`, pressing `Ctrl+C` sends SIGINT to PID 1 and **stops the container** (unless the process handles it gracefully).

To **detach without stopping**, use the escape sequence:

```
Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Q
```

This returns you to your host terminal while keeping the container running.

> Some containers may not support this if they don’t handle the escape sequence correctly.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `--sig-proxy=false`

If you want `Ctrl+C` to work locally without affecting the container, attach with:
```bash
docker attach --sig-proxy=false my-container
```
Now `Ctrl+C` detaches gracefully without stopping the container.

slides.title: attach Example 📺
slides.content: Start a counter in the background and attach to see its output:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Start a script that prints every second
docker run -d --name counter alpine sh -c 'i=1; while true; do echo $i; i=$((i+1)); sleep 1; done'

# Attach to see the numbers
docker attach counter

# Detach with Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Q
# Container keeps running

docker ps

quizData.question: What key sequence detaches from a container without stopping it?
quizData.explanation: `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+Q` is the default detach sequence. `Ctrl+C` would stop the container, and `Ctrl+D` usually exits the shell.
